}}'''Toby Stephen Gee''' {{post-nominals|FRS}} (born 2 January 1980) is a British [[mathematician]] working in number theory and arithmetic aspects of the [[Langlands program|Langlands Program]].  He specialises in [[algebraic number theory]].

Gee was awarded the [[Whitehead Prize]] in 2012,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/files/reports/LMS_Prizes_2012.pdf|title=Prizes 2012|website=London Mathematical Society}}</ref> the [[Leverhulme Prize]] in 2012,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leverhulme.ac.uk/sites/default/files/imported_pdfs/2012%20prize%20winners%20+%20citations.pdf|title=Philip Leverhulme Prize Winners 2012|website=The Leverhulme Trust}}</ref> and was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2014<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/fellows2014.pdf|title=2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|website=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> and of the Royal Society in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Outstanding scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2024/05/new-fellows-2024/ |access-date=2024-05-18 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Gee read mathematics at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], where he was [[Senior Wrangler]] in 2000. After completing his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] with [[Kevin Buzzard]] at [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]] in 2004, he was a Benjamin Peirce Assistant Professor at [[Harvard University]] until 2010. From 2010 to 2011 Gee was an assistant professor at [[Northwestern University]], at which point he moved to Imperial College London, where he has been a professor since 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ma.imperial.ac.uk/~tsg/Index_files/cv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|publisher=Imperial College|access-date=2024-04-07}}</ref>

With [[Mark Kisin]], he proved the Breuil–Mézard conjecture for potentially Barsotti–Tate representations,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gee|first1=Toby|last2=Kisin|first2=Mark|date=December 2014|title=The Breuil–Mézard Conjecture For Potentially Barsotti–Tate Representations|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/forum-of-mathematics-pi/article/the-breuilmezard-conjecture-for-potentially-barsottitate-representations/6DCF8D6D14C7CACFFBAAF58B1B006AD9|journal=Forum of Mathematics, Pi|language=en|volume=2|doi=10.1017/fmp.2014.1|issn=2050-5086|arxiv=1208.3179|s2cid=16351884}}</ref> and with [[Thomas Barnet-Lamb]] and David Geraghty, he proved the [[Sato–Tate conjecture]] for [[Hilbert modular form]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Barnet-Lamb|first1=Thomas|last2=Gee|first2=Toby|last3=Geraghty|first3=David|date=2011|title=The Sato–Tate conjecture for Hilbert modular forms|url=https://www.ams.org/home/page/|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|language=en-US|volume=24|issue=2|pages=411–469|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-2010-00689-3|issn=0894-0347|arxiv=0912.1054|s2cid=12534084}}</ref> One of his most influential ideas has been the introduction of a general 'philosophy of weights', which has clarified some aspects of the emerging mod ''p'' Langlands philosophy.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2013-04-01|title=Prizewinners 2012|url=https://academic.oup.com/blms/article/45/2/421/295290|journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society|language=en|volume=45|issue=2|pages=421–428|doi=10.1112/blms/bdt015|s2cid=247674468 |issn=0024-6093|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
